task: Make one bounded security repair on current main for the writable request-branch trust-boundary flaw in BOTH ChatGPT production ops paths: `.github/workflows/chatgpt-ops.yml` (`chatgpt-ops-requests`, environment `hetzner-operator`) and `.github/workflows/chatgpt-ed-new-ops.yml` (`chatgpt-ed-new-ops-requests`, environment `ed-new-operator`). Do not access or deploy to production. Current flaw: push-triggered privileged workflows execute the workflow definition from the writable request branch, so a modified workflow revision can consume operator environment secrets; checking out trusted main later does not fix the workflow-definition trust boundary. Refactor to a safe two-stage design analogous to the Codex dispatcher: request-branch push workflow(s) must be secret-free/environment-free and only validate a single bounded JSON request then dispatch a privileged executor workflow on trusted `main` via `workflow_dispatch` (or an equivalently safe protected-ref mechanism). The privileged executor workflow(s) must be `workflow_dispatch` only, run from `main`, keep the existing operation allowlists and exact environment boundaries, and never execute privileged code from the request ref. Preserve the connector-friendly JSON request paths and current manual workflow_dispatch UX if practical. Also fix the existing push-range fragility (multi-commit push / branch-creation zero before SHA) in the request dispatcher rather than relying on fetch-depth 2, and add structural regression tests proving: request-branch workflow code has no operator environments/secrets; privileged executors cannot be push-triggered; dispatch targets `ref: main`; only one allowlisted request JSON may drive a dispatch; and a previously modified request-branch workflow cannot gain operator secrets. Review the fixed concurrency behavior too: do not silently drop a middle request merely because multiple operations queue; if the current fixed concurrency group can replace pending requests, use a durable/unique dispatch strategy while preserving safe production serialization at the privileged execution boundary. Preserve all existing fail-closed operation guards, pinned known-host trust already present on ed-new, no DB/volume/migration/env broadening, and existing operator receipts. For the legacy Hetzner path, do not introduce new trust-on-first-use; if current repository contracts already provide a pinned known-hosts secret, use it rather than ssh-keyscan, otherwise leave host-key behavior unchanged and report the limitation instead of inventing a secret. Update canonical control-plane docs if needed so advertised operations match reality. Run focused workflow/ops/security contract tests, YAML parse, relevant pytest/Ruff, and git diff --check. Push only the bounded implementation branch; do not merge.
